templates.why_chosen: High-confidence pipeline in the fan-out/fan-in variant: a trapezoid connector splits Metadata across 16 identical Pipe Manager boxes elided with a vertical ellipsis, while a separate lower lane carries bulk Data to the same DMA Engine.
templates.what_to_learn: Use trapezoid connectors, not sixteen arrows, to fan data to and from N identical replicated boxes, elide the middle instances with a vertical ellipsis, and keep the bulk-data lane physically separate from the control lane; draw side-channel control inputs thinner so they are not mistaken for the main dataflow.

templates.why_chosen: Canonical fan-in coordinator-over-replicas: 16 identical RX Pipe Manager trapezoids, elided with a vertical ellipsis, converge into one Notification Buffer Manager, while a separate parallel lane keeps the bulk Data FIFO independent of that metadata fan-in.
templates.what_to_learn: Fan-in works the same as fan-out: converge 16 elided, identical processing units into one shared manager using trapezoid connectors, and route a second kind of payload (bulk data) through its own separate, differently-shaped lane so the two never look like the same pipeline.

templates.why_chosen: High-confidence rank-22 pick for the times-N rule: sixteen identical RX pipe-manager boxes are elided to two with a vertical ellipsis between them, and bulk data runs in its own FIFO lane beside the metadata path.
templates.what_to_learn: Draw only the first and last of a large identical bank, two of sixteen pipe managers, linked by a vertical ellipsis instead of drawing every copy, and give bulk data its own narrow FIFO lane beside the control path; this figure blurs MMIO control arrows with dataflow arrows, so mark control inputs distinctly.
